evidence: The programmatic Alembic registry accepts only the exact fingerprinted version-1 predecessor and applies one ordered forward-only 0002_schema_history revision inside the caller-owned SQLite transaction.

Before revision execution, the runner obtains a writer reservation, verifies complete WAL checkpointing, creates a second-connection SQLite online backup under stable held Windows paths, reopens it against the exact source profile, and publishes a schema-valid immutable recovery manifest bound to the backup bytes and source/target fingerprints.

A deterministic failure after every migration DDL statement rolls the source back to exact version-1 schema/data semantics, retains the verified backup and bounded failure record, and a later retry succeeds. Fresh/current version-2 detection is idempotent and creates no backup.
The exact supported prior-schema inventory contains version 1 only; both the dry-run and full backup/migrate/recover paths execute against that frozen fixture.

Eight dedicated migration tests plus the existing nine storage tests cover success, dry-run, rollback, retry/restart, lock contention, wrong location/version/fingerprint, redirected backup roots, live backup/manifest write denial, and ordinary forged history mutations.

The real frozen package is built and inspected, not mocked: Alembic operations, SQLAlchemy engine support, the migration runner, and the exact governed revision are all present and loadable without system Python.
The stable Core --check response contract is preserved; migration-runtime loadability is exercised internally and archive identity proves the new runtime is shipped.

The portable SQLite profile advances to schema version 2 with exact table/trigger/profile fingerprints; the new recovery-manifest schema, storage documentation, Core/package documentation, build-input inventory, quality scope, and locked dependencies are updated together.

Alembic 1.18.5 and SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 are exact direct locks. The final scanner report identifies their transitive Python set and all five new-package license findings as ALLOW with no new blocking finding.

No UI/reference content, project-lifecycle mutation workflow, repository implementation, encryption, object storage, or unrelated capability behavior was added; T03 remains responsible for typed repositories and units of work.
